body.statement: For every \(p\ge2\), the one-root star construction contains a nonempty strict-inequality parameter region on which the pairwise rank matrix \(R\) is invariant under swapping the baseline with the root-intervention vertex. Consequently, no component-permutation-equivariant rank-only selector universally recovers the baseline on \(\mathcal M_p\).
body.justification: The obstruction shows that the correction needs entrywise support and marginal information, rather than a different scalar aggregation of the same ranks.
body.gap: Squires et al. use one rank score, but the literature does not establish an open-family impossibility for the entire class of equivariant rank-only selectors.
body.consumer: Method designers can rule out every rank-only baseline heuristic and focus on information-preserving summaries.
body.proof_tex:
Fix \(p\geq 2\) and a member of the one-root star family in
\(\texttt{def:star-counterfamily}\).  Thus vertex \(1\) is the root, and,
for each \(j\in\{2,\ldots,p\}\), the only edge into \(j\) is
\(1\to j\), with coefficient \(b_j\neq 0\).  Consequently the transposes
of the structural-equation rows are
\[
 a_1=e_1,
 \qquad
 a_j=e_j-b_j e_1\quad (j=2,\ldots,p).
\]
All baseline and intervention variances are strictly positive by the
definition of the family.  Put
\[
 d=\tau_1^{-1}-\omega_1^{-1}.
\]
The root intervention is effective precisely as required here because
\(d\neq 0\).  By \(\texttt{lem:surgery-identity}\),
\[
 \Delta_1=d e_1e_1^{\top}.                                      \tag{1}
\]
For a leaf \(j\geq 2\), the same identity gives
\[
 \Delta_j
 =\tau_j^{-1}e_je_j^{\top}
  -\omega_j^{-1}(e_j-b_je_1)(e_j-b_je_1)^{\top}.                 \tag{2}
\]
Hence \(\Delta_j\) vanishes off the rows and columns indexed by
\(\{1,j\}\), and its principal matrix on those coordinates is
\[
 \left.\Delta_j\right|_{\{1,j\}}
 =
 \begin{pmatrix}
 -b_j^2/\omega_j & b_j/\omega_j\\
 b_j/\omega_j & \tau_j^{-1}-\omega_j^{-1}
 \end{pmatrix}.                                                  \tag{3}
\]
Direct expansion, using \(b_j\neq0\), \(\omega_j>0\), and
\(\tau_j>0\), yields
\[
 \det\!\left(\left.\Delta_j\right|_{\{1,j\}}\right)
 =-\frac{b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}<0.                              \tag{4}
\]
It follows from (4) that
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_0)
 =\operatorname{rank}(\Delta_j)=2.                              \tag{5}
\]
Likewise, subtracting (1) from (3) and expanding gives
\[
 \det\!\left(
   \left.(\Delta_j-\Delta_1)\right|_{\{1,j\}}
 \right)
 =\frac{d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2}{\omega_j\tau_j}.              \tag{6}
\]
The strict inequality in \(\texttt{def:star-counterfamily}\) makes the
numerator in (6) negative, so it is nonzero.  Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(K_j-K_1)
 =\operatorname{rank}(\Delta_j-\Delta_1)=2.                     \tag{7}
\]
Finally, (1) and \(d\neq0\) imply
\[
 \operatorname{rank}(K_1-K_0)=1.                                \tag{8}
\]

Let \(\sigma\) be the transposition of component vertices \(0\) and
\(1\).  Equations (5) and (7) say that, for every leaf-intervention
vertex \(j\geq2\),
\[
 R_{0j}=R_{1j}=2,
\]
while (8) gives \(R_{01}=R_{10}=1\).  Entries whose two indices are leaf
vertices are unchanged by \(\sigma\), simply because \(\sigma\) fixes
both indices.  The diagonal entries are zero.  These cases exhaust the
entries of \(R\), and hence, with \(P_\sigma\) the permutation matrix of
\(\sigma\),
\[
 P_\sigma R P_\sigma^{\top}=R.                                  \tag{9}
\]

The strict region used above is nonempty and open relative to the
continuous parameter space of this fixed star graph.  Indeed, take
\[
 \omega_k=1\quad(k\in V),\qquad
 \tau_1=2,\qquad
 \tau_j=1\quad(j\geq2),\qquad
 b_j=1\quad(j\geq2).
\]
Then \(d=-1/2\), and for every leaf
\[
 d(\tau_j-\omega_j)-b_j^2=-1<0.
\]
All variances are positive, the root variance changes, and every leaf
has a nonzero parent coefficient.  Thus all interventions are effective,
including the leaf interventions whose intervention variance equals their
baseline noise variance.  Positivity, \(d\neq0\), nonzero coefficients,
and the finitely many displayed strict inequalities persist on a
neighborhood by continuity.  By \(\texttt{def:model-class}\), that
neighborhood lies in \(\mathcal M_p\).

Now let \(F\) be any rank-only baseline selector that is equivariant under
permutations of the component vertices.  By
\(\texttt{def:rank-compression}\), equivariance means
\[
 F(P_\gamma R P_\gamma^{\top})=\gamma(F(R))                     \tag{10}
\]
for every component permutation \(\gamma\).  Applying (10) with
\(\gamma=\sigma\) and using (9) gives
\[
 F(R)=\sigma(F(R)).                                              \tag{11}
\]
Neither \(0\) nor \(1\) is fixed by \(\sigma\).  Thus (11) implies in
particular that \(F(R)\neq0\), although component \(0\) is the
observational baseline.  The selector therefore fails at every point of
the nonempty open family.  Since \(F\) was arbitrary, no
component-permutation-equivariant rank-only selector universally recovers
the baseline on \(\mathcal M_p\).

For completeness, this obstruction is not confined to the
observed-coordinate subclass of the model in Squires et al.~
\cite[Appendix F.2, Proposition 10]{pmlr-v202-squires23a}.  We verify the
required restriction to their full published domain explicitly.  In the
notation of that model, take latent dimension \(d=p\), observation and
mixing matrices \(G_{\mathrm{Sq}}=I_p\) and
\(H_{\mathrm{Sq}}=I_p\), and define the normalized mechanism matrices
\[
 \mathcal B_0=\Omega^{-1/2}A,
 \qquad
 \mathcal B_j
 =\mathcal B_0
  +e_j\bigl(\tau_j^{-1/2}e_j-\mathcal B_0^{\top}e_j\bigr)^{\top}
 \quad(j\in V).                                                  \tag{12}
\]
The matrix \(\Omega^{-1/2}\) in (12) is well defined because \(\Omega\)
is diagonal with strictly positive entries.
The additive term in (12) has only row \(j\) nonzero.  Moreover,
\[
 e_j^{\top}\mathcal B_j
 =e_j^{\top}\mathcal B_0
  +\tau_j^{-1/2}e_j^{\top}-e_j^{\top}\mathcal B_0
 =\tau_j^{-1/2}e_j^{\top},                                      \tag{13}
\]
whereas every other row agrees with \(\mathcal B_0\).  Thus (12) is
exactly the normalized single-row perfect intervention allowed by the
published class.  It is nontrivial: for a nonroot, the baseline row has a
nonzero parent entry, while for a root effectiveness gives
\(\tau_j\neq\omega_j\), so in both cases
\(\mathcal B_j\neq\mathcal B_0\).  A topological ordering makes \(A\)
unit triangular; deleting the off-diagonal entries of one row leaves it
unit triangular.  Consequently \(\mathcal B_0\) and every
\(\mathcal B_j\) are nonsingular, using the strict positivity of all
variances.

Writing the baseline row vectors as above, (12)--(13) imply
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \mathcal B_0^{\top}\mathcal B_0
 &=A^{\top}\Omega^{-1}A
  =\Sigma_0^{-1}=K_0,\\
 \mathcal B_j^{\top}\mathcal B_j
 &=\sum_{k\neq j}\omega_k^{-1}a_ka_k^{\top}
   +\tau_j^{-1}e_je_j^{\top}
  =(A^{(j)})^{\top}(\Omega^{(j)})^{-1}A^{(j)}
  =\Sigma_j^{-1}=K_j.                                           \tag{14}
 \end{aligned}
\]
Here the inverse equalities follow respectively from
\(\texttt{ass:baseline-gaussian-sem}\) and
\(\texttt{ass:perfect-single-node-surgeries}\), with invertibility just
verified.  Because \(G_{\mathrm{Sq}}=H_{\mathrm{Sq}}=I_p\), the
published precision objects satisfy
\(\Theta_j=\mathcal B_j^{\top}\mathcal B_j=K_j\).  Therefore every
member of \(\mathcal M_p\), and in particular the open star family above,
embeds into the full Proposition-10 class with exactly the same pairwise
rank matrix.  A selector universally correct on that full class would
restrict to a universally correct selector on the embedded star family,
contradicting (11).  Hence no component-permutation-equivariant rank-only
selector universally recovers the observational context on the full
Squires Proposition-10 class.  This transferred negative conclusion does
not assert positive recovery under latent mixing.
